provenance: Read-only source-paired Tshivenda assessment draft from the current canonical and VE registry. Ordinary framing is proposed for facilitator review; technical terms and uncertain clauses remain exact English. No repository files or learner wiring changed.

keyPoints: Record seed identity, source and quality, and check if permission is needed before sharing
Agree care, booking and repair responsibilities for shared tools
Measure losses and net returns for each selling route
Combine shared experience with qualified help when needed
questions: Neighbours want to share saved seed. What helps make the shared seed useful?
A grower is comparing a distant market with nearby customers. What should guide the decision?
options: Agree seed-quality checks and check whether permission is needed to share the variety
Assume sharing automatically improves every seed lot
Rely only on the size of the group
Always choose the highest headline price
Compare money received after fees, transport, unsold produce and losses
Assume joining a group removes all costs
rationales: Seed quality depends on crop-specific isolation, selection, labelling, storage and germination checks. Those checks do not establish permission to exchange a protected variety; check the applicable rights before sharing.
Distance affects costs, but it is not the only factor. Use actual returns and losses to compare the options.
